meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Egypt (Cairo; no sub-state corporate tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified, French-inspired; Islamic Sharia is a residual source under Article 2 of the 2014 Constitution; commercial matters governed by the Commercial Code No. 17 of 1999 and Companies Law No. 159 of 1981)

Egypt-United Kingdom Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (1975)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing as amended by Laws No. 78 of 2003, No. 181 of 2008, No. 36 of 2014 and No. 194 of 2020; AML Executive Regulations (Prime Ministerial Decree No. 157 of 2003 as amended); Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU) directives; Central Bank of Egypt Unified AML/CFT Rules (as updated); Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 as amended by Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and Law No. 148 of 2019, including the mandatory Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) register and disclosure requirements administered by the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the passport of each founding individual shareholder and each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority / Ministry of Interior of the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Egypt is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention of 1961; legalization by the Egyptian Embassy/Consulate in the country of issuance is required)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (recent utility bill or bank account statement dated within 3 months) for each foreign founder and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility company or banking institution of the shareholder's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference / financial standing letter confirming the funding capacity of each foreign founder
Certificate of good standing / incumbency certificate for any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or competent corporate authority of the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney (Arabic/English) authorizing the incorporation counsel and GAFI agent to file and execute incorporation documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the founder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization plus subsequent Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) recognition upon submission

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all founders, UBOs, directors and authorized signatories against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, Egyptian EMLCU domestic terrorist financing and sanctions lists, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List and UK HMT Consolidated List. PEP status determination (domestic and foreign) is required with risk-based Enhanced Due Diligence, source-of-funds verification and senior-management approval for higher-risk profiles. Screening must be re-run within 7 business days before notarization of the incorporation contract and thereafter on an ongoing trigger-event basis under Law No. 80 of 2002 and CBE AML/CFT Rules.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI (General Authority for Investment and Free Zones) One-Stop-Shop e-Portal and Commercial Registration e-Services - https://www.gafi.gov.eg / https://www.investinegypt.gov.eg
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be registered in Arabic script as the primary official name; a Latin/English transliteration matching the Arabic phonetically is permitted as an alternative name. The name must reflect the permitted commercial activity and must not mislead as to the company's legal form. The suffix indicating limited liability (LLC / Sharikat Dhat Mas'uliyya Mahduda - 'LLC' or 'ذ.م.م') is mandatory. Arabic diacritics, numerals, special symbols and purely descriptive generic terms without a distinctive element are rejected.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank / بنك (requires prior Central Bank of Egypt approval)
Securities / أوراق مالية (requires prior FRA license)
Egypt - Arab Republic of Egypt / جمهورية مصر العربية (requires prior Cabinet-level authorization)
Pharmaceutical / أدوية (requires prior Egyptian Drug Authority approval)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A rejected name may be challenged by submitting a written administrative appeal to the GAFI Legal Affairs Department (Company Applications Division) within 15 days of the rejection notice, accompanied by a justification memorandum and, if applicable, a revised name. An immediate re-filing of a modified distinctive name via the GAFI e-portal is permitted. If the rejection is based on public-policy grounds or the refusal of a sensitive-token approval, a further appeal may be filed before the Egyptian State Council Administrative Court within 60 days under the State Council Law No. 47 of 1972. Fees for the appeal are nominal (approximately USD 10-20) and a GAFI response is expected within 15 business days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not acceptable as a standalone solution. GAFI and the Commercial Registry require a physical, verifiable Egyptian head-office address for service of process and statutory correspondence. A dedicated-desk serviced office or co-working space with a written lease of at least one year, a physical reception, and documented right to receive official mail may satisfy the requirement on a case-by-case basis. Pure virtual mailbox addresses are rejected.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low in the base case but non-trivial: approximately 5% annual probability in the first year of operation, increasing to 15-20% if the company becomes subject to VAT registration, income tax audit, or AML/CFT queries from the ETA, GAFI or the EMLCU regarding commercial substance and the physical presence of the registered office.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended by Law No. 4 of 2009 (LLC regime, Articles 1-104); Executive Regulations of the Companies Law issued by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 540 of 1982; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 for GAFI registration procedures
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI), Companies Registration Department / One-Stop-Shop, Egyptian Ministry of Investment and International Cooperation
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association of the Limited Liability Company (Ta'sis Contract and Nizam Al-Ta'sis)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Egyptian LLC law sets no fixed statutory minimum paid-up capital; GAFI practice requires a stated capital compatible with the intended software-platform scope, with the capital fully subscribed and deposited into a bank escrow/non-operational account opened in the name of the company under formation, released only after issuance of the Commercial Register extract
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: The Articles of Association submitted to this First Board Meeting, and signed by all founding members, is adopted as the Company's definitive governing document under Law No. 159 of 1981. RESOLVED: The allocation, subscription, and allotment of the issued shares set forth in the subscription schedule are approved, and the paid-up capital shall be deposited into the designated incorporation escrow bank account of the Company under formation. RESOLVED: The registered office at [Cairo, Egypt] is approved as the Company's statutory domicile for service of process and regulatory correspondence. RESOLVED: [________] is appointed Senior Manager and [________] is appointed Finance Manager, each vested with full authority to complete all incorporation filings, publish statutory notices, and open corporate banking facilities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Reservation and Pre-Registration Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop-Shop / Companies Registration Department electronic portal (Invest in Egypt)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a corporate name reservation application through the GAFI online investor platform. The proposed Arabic and English names must be distinct from existing registered Egyptian entities and must not include terms contrary to public order. Upon approval, obtain the official name clearance certificate, which is valid for a defined reservation period during which incorporation must be filed.
required_dossiers: Copy of valid national ID or passport of each founding member
Power of attorney (if a founder acts through an agent)
Proposed name in Arabic and English
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for conflicts or similarity, file an administrative objection with the GAFI Name Committee within 15 days, or reserve an amended name through the same portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Articles of Association (Ta'sis Contract)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public Department (Shahr Al-Aqari), Egyptian Ministry of Justice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Have all founding members appear in person before the notary public, or through duly authorized attorneys, to execute the Ta'sis Contract and Nizam Al-Ta'sis. The notary will verify identities, confirm legal capacity, and certify the signatures. The notarized incorporation document constitutes the statutory formation instrument for registration.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
Valid national ID or passport of each founding member
Consent of the registered office property owner, if not a founder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries the drafting or identity documents, correct the deficiencies and re-apply for notarization; unresolved refusals may be escalated as a complaint to the Ministry of Justice Notarial Oversight Administration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the Escrow Capital Account and Paid-Up Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Egyptian commercial bank (e.g., National Bank of Egypt, Banque Misr, CIB) acting as the capital escrow institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a special non-operational account titled to the company under formation. Each founding member transfers or deposits the subscribed share amounts. The bank issues a certificate of capital deposit confirming the paid-up capital balance, which is a mandatory attachment for the GAFI incorporation file.
required_dossiers: Lease contract or proof of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires enhanced due diligence, provide supplementary KYC and source-of-funds evidence; if the account is refused, transfer the opening request to another licensed Egyptian bank and renew the deposit certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI Statutory Incorporation Filing and Commercial Register Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Companies Registration Department / One-Stop-Shop (Invest in Egypt portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete incorporation file through the GAFI one-stop-shop, physically or electronically, including the notarized Ta'sis Contract, capital deposit certificate, registered office proof, and GAFI standard forms. Pay the stamp duty, notarization fee and registration fee. Upon approval, GAFI issues the Commercial Register extract and the company acquires juridical personality.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Lease contract or deed for the registered office
GAFI incorporation application and statutory forms for founders and managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to GAFI examiners' technical queries within the stipulated deadline and provide supplementary documents; any formal rejection may be appealed to the GAFI legal settlement and grievance unit within 30 days of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Incorporation Abstract in the Commercial Gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Official Commercial Gazette (Al-Waqa'i Al-Misriyya), Egyptian Ministry of Justice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After issuance of the Commercial Register extract, file the statutory abstract of incorporation with the Commercial Gazette for publication. The published notice must list the company's name, object, capital, registered office, and managers. Retain the newspaper edition and payment receipt for the post-registration compliance file.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the gazette prints erroneous information, apply immediately for a rectification notice and pay the associated correction fee; late publication may be cured by filing an explanatory note with GAFI.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Tax, Social Insurance and Operational License Facilitation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA); National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI); GAFI One-Stop-Shop for the unified activity licence
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the post-incorporation registrations: obtain the ETA tax card and VAT certificate (where turnover exceeds the registration threshold), register employees with NOSI for social insurance, and secure the unified economic activity licence (Al-Rukhsa Al-Muwahhada) issued through GAFI covering the esports platform office operations. Activation of global payment rails (Stripe/PayPal) is contracted after the commercial license is issued.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resolve any disqualification by correcting declarations and paying assessed fines; decisions of the ETA may be contested before the internal tax appeal committee, and GAFI licensing refusals may be referred to the GAFI grievance department.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: N/A - non-industrial activity; no Industrial Development Authority (IDA) licence required. The GAFI One-Stop-Shop issues the unified economic activity licence for the software publishing and esports platform scope.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Unified Economic Activity Licence (Al-Rukhsa Al-Muwahhada) issued by GAFI; local civil defense and health clearances where a physical office is operated

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA), Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category (C) - Exempt from full EIA study; only a general environmental registration note is required for office-based software publishing activities under Law 4 of 1994, as amended, and Executive Regulation Decree No. 338 of 1995
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC or flue-gas emission limits apply to this ISIC 5820 scope; obligations are limited to municipal wastewater compliance for office sanitary discharge, EEAA-regulated e-waste handling through licensed waste contractors, and general noise and air-quality conditions applicable to office premises.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense Organization fire-safety clearance for the registered office (fire extinguishers, emergency exits, electrical inspection and evacuation plan); workplace health and safety certification under Law 12 of 2003 (Labour Law) verified by the Ministry of Manpower; and structural/electrical load inspection clearance for the leased premises under the Egyptian Building Code.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance – e-Tax and e-Invoicing portals available via www.eta.gov.eg and the ETA electronic invoicing system at einvoice.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-incorporated shareholder establishes the Egyptian LLC through the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) or the Commercial Registry, then applies to the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) for the unified Tax ID and Tax Card. The LLC must submit its audited memorandum of association, commercial registration certificate, articles of incorporation, valid passports/POAs of shareholders and managers, lease/contract for the registered office, and other ETA-prescribed forms. Non-resident shareholders without a permanent establishment may register separately only for VAT and withholding purposes if making taxable supplies of digital services or deriving Egyptian-source payments.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt does not provide a check-the-box election. The Egyptian LLC is treated as a separate legal person, not a pass-through vehicle. There are no hybrid mismatch or fiscal unity elections available for this LLC; entity classification is determined solely under Egyptian commercial and tax law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual value of taxable supplies; voluntary registration is available for persons supplying above EGP 50,000 per calendar year
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time electronic invoicing with integrated ETA clearance: qualifying taxpayers must transmit invoices in a simplified digital format to the ETA e-invoicing system through approved APIs, receive an ETA clearance number, and imprint a machine-readable QR code on each issued invoice. B2C transactions are progressively covered by the e-receipt system. Non-compliance with e-invoicing/clearance requirements triggers administrative penalties and customs/vAT refund delays.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available for goods physically exported from Egypt, for international transport services connected therewith, and for services supplied to a non-resident recipient to the extent the service is provided from Egypt and effectively used and consumed outside Egypt. The supplier must hold statutory export documentation in compliance with Law 67 of 2016 and ETA issuing rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Valid Customs Export Declaration cleared by the Egyptian Customs Authority through the automated customs system
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure of the goods from Egypt
Inward Foreign Remittance Certificate or Egyptian bank statement proving receipt of export proceeds in convertible foreign currency
Commercial invoice, underlying sales contract, and VAT return annexure referencing the export customs declarations
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA may refuse or claw back any zero-rated VAT benefit where the exporter fails to prove physical export, the services are not effectively consumed outside Egypt, or the foreign currency consideration is not repatriated within 180 days. Non-compliant claims are reassessed at the standard 14% VAT rate, with statutory late-payment additional tax of 2% per month or fraction thereof, plus potential doubling of tax liability, denial of VAT refunds, criminal fines and imprisonment for fraudulent evasion, and extension of the statute of limitations in cases of fictitious exports or forged documentation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) - Al-Bank Al-Markazi Al-Masry
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a unified market-clearing floating exchange-rate regime for the EGP introduced on 6 March 2024, replacing the crisis-era rationed FX system and unifying the official and parallel rates. Current-account payments are broadly freely convertible consistent with Egypt's IMF Article VIII obligations accepted in 2009. Capital-account convertibility is conditioned on proper banking-channel documentation: dividend, profit, interest and capital-gains remittances require completion of underlying bank verification, evidence of FDI registration with the General Authority for Investment (GAFI) under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, and in most cases an Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) tax-clearance certificate confirming settlement of applicable corporate and distribution taxes. Practical profit-remittance hurdles are procedural rather than quantitative: banks require source-of-funds documentation, updated commercial-register extracts, a board resolution authorising the distribution, evidence that the LLC has filed annual tax returns, and clearing of any related-party transfer-pricing reporting obligations; overseas payments are then routed via SWIFT without CBE prior approval. Companies should further ensure the foreign shareholder is recorded in the GAFI/e-investment registry and the capital has been fully paid-in through banking channels to avoid blocking of reinvestment or dividend outward remittances.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBE policy, export proceeds from goods and services must be repatriated into Egypt through an Egyptian banking channel within 90 days from the date of the bill of lading for goods or from the invoice/service-completion date for services; CBE approval can extend the window for documented justified delay. Following the March 2024 FX liberalisation, the mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts is effectively 0%: exporters may retain 100% of proceeds in foreign-currency accounts at Egyptian banks, and the previous crisis-era surrender-to-EGP requirement has been abolished. The operative regulatory duties are (i) full repatriation through authorised banks, (ii) truthful attribution of the BOP purpose code and underlying trade documentation, and (iii) consistency between the invoiced value, shipping documents and the credited amount; unrepatriated proceeds or mismatched invoices will be treated as an AML/CFT compliance breach and may trigger bank account suspension.

Operational EGP Account; FCY Retention Account; Cash-Management Treasury Facility

Multi-Currency Current Account; Cross-Border Settlement and Correspondent Banking Facility

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW-MEDIUM. Egyptian law, principally CBE Law No. 194 of 2020 on Fintech and the CBE payment-systems framework, requires any payment-service, digital-wallet or closed-loop clearing activity to be performed by a CBE-licensed provider; an offshore EMI (e.g., a Wise/Payoneer-style digital bank) has no autonomous authorisation to open bank accounts, clear payments, or perform FX conversions inside Egypt and is not recognised by the CBE as a settlement counterparty. Foreign EMIs may integrate only as a technical sub-processor or as the offshore collection entity of a licensed Egyptian PSP. For this esports platform, domestic EGP collections should be cleared through a licensed PSP such as Paymob, fawry, Tap Payments or Mo'amalat, while offshore USD/EUR collections can be received via a non-resident affiliated entity or the Egyptian bank's own correspondent network; reliance on a pure offshore EMI without a local licensed PSP will trigger adverse bank KYC review and is not a viable treasury rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under CBE AML/CFT circulars implementing AML Law No. 80 of 2002, as amended, a physical presence and in-person KYC interview is effectively mandatory at initial account opening: at least one director or the registered authorised signatory must appear before the bank's compliance officer at a branch, or the bank may send a compliance officer to visit the company premises for a face-to-face due-diligence interview. Remote/video-KYC opening is permitted only where the applicant is already an existing banking client with a completed CDD file and a satisfactory transactional history; even then the bank will require original or certified copies of the board resolution appointing signatories, the notarised and legalised memorandum of association, the commercial-register extract, GAFI documents, and complete UBO disclosure for any natural person holding or indirectly controlling more than 25% of the LLC.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign direct ownership with a multi-tier non-resident UBO chain: bank flags source-of-wealth and source-of-funds as unverifiable and demands secondary-source documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: GAFI investment certificate; certified commercial-register extract with full corporate genealogy; updated memorandum of association; UBO register identifying each natural person above the 25% threshold; bank reference letters from UBO home banks; two years of audited financial statements of each material UBO; sworn source-of-wealth declaration supported by portfolio and tax records; and an LLC board resolution appointing Egyptian signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border tournament prize pay-outs to players, teams and coaches (payments to third parties not named on the principal contract) creating a transaction-laundering or false-payment suspicion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed prize-payment schedule; official tournament rulebook disclaiming any concealment; player registration forms with passport or national-ID copies and AML/KYC screening results; executed prize agreements naming the beneficiary; segregation of prize-pool wallets from operational cash; monthly payment-velocity and jurisdiction-disbursement analysis to the bank; standing instruction excluding disbursements to sanctions-flagged or high-risk jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Online payment-processing relationships with international PSPs (Stripe/PayPal as targeted rails): bank decries undisclosed acquirer relationships, chargeback refund flows and unregulated digital transactional exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed merchant agreements with each PSP; PSP registration and tax evidence (VAT/ETAX certificates); settlement-clearing flow charts showing PSP capture-to-bank settlement; binding written representation that PSPs act solely as payment facilitators and never as banking counterparties; confirmed zero cryptocurrency conversion or settlement; quarterly chargeback and refund reconciliation statements; business-model narrative explaining tournament entry fees and prize funding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection structured as a blended equity-plus-shareholder-loan without CBE 'true underlying' documentation, leading the bank to refuse attribution of incoming funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholders' resolution approving the exact equity-versus-loan mix; signed financing agreements and promissory notes; CBE/GAFI FDI registration forms and inward-wire advice; commercial-register capital-increase minutes; capital-verification certificate from a licensed Egyptian auditor; purpose-code narrative ensuring that remittances are tagged as FDI capital contribution and not external debt; CBE monthly external-debt return notification where shareholder loans exceed applicable thresholds.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: the foreign shareholder executes an SWIFT MT103 wire to the LLC's Egyptian bank account with narrative 'Capital contribution - Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 - [LLC Name]'. The Egyptian bank attributes the receipt under the Foreign Direct Investment BOP purpose code, and, under the post-March-2024 liberalised regime, converts to EGP at the interbank spot rate without CBE prior approval. Compliance steps: (i) file the inward remittance advice and SWIFT reference with the bank's trade desk; (ii) maintain the GAFI FDI registration and update the commercial register; (iii) submit an auditor's capital-verification certificate within 60 days of receipt; (iv) where funds are retained in FCY, evidence the intended operating spend and treasury policy; and (v) for shareholder loans, complete the CBE external-debt return and provide the financing agreement so that bank credit, FX purchase and future repatriation rights are preserved.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: (a) SWIFT MT103 for service-based cross-border disbursements, including tournament prize pools to pre-KYC'd natural-person beneficiaries and payments to foreign tournament operators and cloud-infrastructure providers, each with the relevant BOP purpose code and underlying contract; (b) commercial Letter of Credit at sight (or usance where approved) for hardware/equipment imports requiring title documents to travel via the banking channel; (c) cash-against-documents for low-value cloud gaming, content and licensing purchases; (d) domestic EGP disbursements and user top-ups through CBE-licensed e-payment gateways (Paymob/Fawry ecosystem) with settlement into the platform's pooled EGP account via the CBE-operated EG-Net RTGS system; and (e) USD/EUR clearing through the bank's global correspondent network for final settlement to PSP payees. Renote that Stripe and PayPal are not licensed clearing rails in Egypt; they can be used only as payment facilitators capturing card transactions, with funds ultimately swept via the licensed PSP and Egyptian banking system to the LLC's accounts.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forward (deliverable) on genuine trade or financial underlying, executed with an Egyptian licensed bank and documented per CBE underlying-transaction rules
Cross-Currency Swap benchmarked to matched export/import cash flows or FDI liability servicing, permitted under CBE derivatives framework
Trade-facility hedges and FCY borrowing hedges linked to documentary collections and import LCs

Offshore NDF on EGP: executable only outside Egypt by offshore counterparties, not offered onshore by Egyptian banks; offshore contracts must be separately disclosed for ETA transfer-pricing purposes and are operationally discouraged

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary general meeting approving the financial statements, management report, auditor report, and profit allocation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company partners; no routine filing authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of each financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Potential company-law fines, director or manager liability, and regulatory enforcement; no single automatic strike-off period applies solely to late meeting convening.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and independent auditor report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI), where filing is applicable to the company record
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally within one month after approval by the competent corporate body; confirm the applicable GAFI submission procedure and period for the company record
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Possible administrative fines, filing rejection, regulatory notices, and manager liability; persistent non-compliance may support administrative dissolution proceedings, but no universal automatic strike-off timeline is prescribed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the end of the financial year, generally by 30 April for a calendar-year taxpayer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties, tax assessments, interest or equivalent statutory additions, audit exposure, and collection enforcement under the Egyptian Tax Procedures Law; tax default does not create an automatic corporate strike-off timeline.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of corporate particulars, including registered office, managers, partners, and shareholding changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI and the competent commercial registry, where a change has occurred
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No general annual return equivalent to the United Kingdom filing model; file changes within the applicable statutory period after occurrence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late amendment filing may result in administrative fines, inability to evidence current authority or ownership, and regulatory or commercial-register enforcement; no fixed annual strike-off deadline applies.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An Egyptian LLC is generally required to maintain audited annual financial statements and appoint an auditor licensed in Egypt under the Companies Law framework. Any small-company exemption or simplified treatment must be confirmed against the company's capital, partner count, and current GAFI rules.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards, which are substantially aligned with IFRS; IFRS application should be confirmed with the appointed Egyptian auditor and applicable regulatory requirements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Egypt does not generally prescribe a standalone annual UBO confirmation filing for every LLC. The company should conduct an annual internal confirmation of ultimate ownership and control, update its UBO and partner records promptly after any change, and provide information to competent authorities, banks, and regulated service providers when required under anti-money-laundering rules.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Managers and authorized signatories
General assembly and partners' resolutions minute book
Ultimate beneficial ownership records and supporting ownership documentation

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 1,000-3,500 annually, depending on location, mail handling, local representation, and compliance support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 2,000-8,000 annually for a small operating LLC; higher fees may apply for material revenue, foreign ownership, regulated activities, or complex related-party transactions

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday for ISIC 5820 digital/esports platforms. Targeted relief only: (i) registered projects under Investment Law 72/2017 may deduct up to 50% of invested capital from taxable profits over 7 years (up to 80% for high-priority geographic zones); (ii) SCZONE-licensed projects receive the same investment incentives; (iii) dividends received from Egyptian companies are exempt under Law 91/2005 Art. 51; (iv) foreign tax credit is allowed for foreign withholding taxes on foreign-source income, capped at the Egyptian tax attributable to that income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 41 (Corporate Income Tax Return, 'Bayyanat Dakhla'); filed electronically through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) E-Tax portal at https://www.eta.gov.eg; paper filings accepted only under e-filing exemption letters from the ETA.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 4 months after the close of the tax year; calendar-year taxpayers must file by April 30 of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax period (fiscal year start and end dates), legal identity, tax card number, commercial registry number, GAFI file number, and registered address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a 100% foreign-owned LLC, state the foreign founder's home-jurisdiction tax identification number and the Egyptian GAFI investment file reference; use the LLC's Egyptian tax card number, not the parent's.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue lines: platform commission, tournament entry fees, prize-pool handling margins, sponsorships, digital advertising, and microtransaction income; then the tax-basis income statement with COGS, operating expenses, depreciation, and net profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare all revenue attributable to Egyptian-source activity at gross, without deducting Stripe/PayPal gateway commissions (deductible later as substantiated expense). Foreign players are taxable only if services are economically connected to the Egyptian PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-deductible expenditures (fines, unsubstantiated marketing, excess entertainment, related-party payments without economic substance) and deduction of exempt income (Egyptian-company dividends).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany platform licence fees, software royalties, and management charges paid to the foreign parent are deductible only when supported by transfer-pricing documentation, a valid contract, and demonstrated beneficial ownership; otherwise add back.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses brought forward from the prior five tax years applied against current-year taxable profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses are accepted only if Form 41 was filed for each loss year and the loss register is attached; a foreign parent cannot consolidate its losses into the Egyptian LLC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit multiplied by 22.5%; deduction of the three quarterly advance instalments already paid; application of foreign tax credit; final balance due or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Egyptian LLC is the sole taxpayer on its own profits; payments or distributions to the foreign founder are not deductible. Any balance due must be settled via ETA treasury account transfer and proven by bank receipt.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: B6 - Related-Party Disclosure and TP Declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of related parties, aggregate value of related-party transactions (platform IP royalties, licences, management fees, prize-pool settlements), transfer-pricing method applied, and declaration of Master File/Local File availability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Full Master File and Local File are mandatory when related-party transactions reach or exceed EGP 30 million per year; a simplified Local File is required for EGP 10-30 million; below EGP 10 million, attach a one-page transaction statement. The ETA may demand the files within 30 days.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: fixed fine of EGP 5,000 plus a monthly delay surcharge of 2% on the unremitted tax for each month (or fraction) after the due date; false or incomplete returns attract the tax evasion penalties of 2-5 years' imprisonment and a fine of EGP 10,000 up to double the evaded tax; the ETA may suspend the tax clearance certificate, block e-invoicing, and compel tax payment by executive distraint.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quarterly Advance Corporate Tax Instalment Notice (annex to Form 41); filed electronically through the ETA E-Tax portal with treasury payment vouchers.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly (3 advance instalments during the tax year)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Instalments are due by the end of the 3rd, 6th, and 9th months of the tax year; each instalment equals one-quarter of the previous year's final tax assessment (or 0.6% of annual gross revenue where no prior-year liability exists).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarter number, taxable base adopted from prior-year assessment, instalment amount due, and payment date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the cumulative 75% threshold is met before the final annual return; under-payment accrues the 2% monthly delay surcharge.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Bank transfer receipts and ETA e-payment vouchers evidencing each instalment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the ETA treasury receipts to the April 30 Form 41; missing attachment triggers automatic assessment of the instalment plus surcharges.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Monthly 2% delay surcharge on each unpaid instalment; repeated non-payment justifies immediate distraint, freezing of the LLC's bank accounts, and suspension of the electronic tax card and e-invoice registration.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% - dividends distributed by an Egyptian LLC are exempt from income tax in the hands of shareholders under Law 91/2005 Art. 51; Egypt does not impose a dividend withholding tax at the corporate distribution level, and there is no additional branch-remittance tax on profit repatriation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: For exempt dividends no TRC is usually required, and the exemption is applied directly by the distributing LLC. For other Egyptian-source payments (interest, royalties, service fees) where a DTA reduces the 20% statutory WHT, the non-resident must submit, before or at payment date, (i) a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the residence-state tax authority, apostilled or legalized in accordance with Egypt's accession to the Hague Apostille Convention, (ii) a completed ETA treaty-relief form and beneficial-ownership declaration, and (iii) the underlying intercompany contract. The ETA's International Tax Office reviews the TRC, applies the relevant DTA rate, and either issues a reduced-withholding consent or processes a refund claim; retroactive claims are accepted for the prior five years but are subject to GAAR and substance-over-form scrutiny.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory: 20% WHT on gross Egyptian-source royalties and 20% WHT on gross Egyptian-source interest paid to non-residents without an Egyptian PE (Law 91/2005 Arts. 45, 56, and 78, as applied under the Unified Tax Procedures Law 174/2020). Typical DTA relief: royalties 10-15% (e.g., Germany 10%, Netherlands 12%, UK 10-12%); interest 8-15% (e.g., Germany 10%, Netherlands 10-15%). Reduced treaty rates apply only if the recipient is the beneficial owner and holds the required TRC and substance evidence.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: No standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) statute is enacted in Egypt; substantive equivalent is enforced through the General Anti-Avoidance Rules (Unified Tax Procedures Law 174/2020 Art. 57 and Law 91/2005 Arts. 40, 57) and the beneficial-ownership doctrine. An Egyptian LLC owning the esports platform IP or booking intercompany prize-pool fees without an Egyptian office, Egyptian employees, active management, and genuine risk assumption may be disregarded by the ETA, which can reattribute income to the foreign parent, reject the 0% dividend exemption, and assess at 22.5% plus the 2% monthly delay surcharge.
